obligations.note: The new branch in purge_due skips every closed payee with category 'tax_authority', so their NPI is never purged after the approved 84-month retention period. That deviates from RET-1, and no legal-hold basis or exception covers it. The sample-coverage control test passing cannot outweigh a deviation that is plain in the code.
The change deviates from RET-1, but the register has no exception for RET-1 or payments.retention. The only exceptions cover SES-1 (expired), LOG-1 (mortgage.logging) and MFA-1 (withdrawn).
Ticket CHG-25709 (standard) was approved by change manager Erik Brandt at 2026-10-09T00:54Z, before the PR opened. Its components (payments.retention) cover the only touched file, retention.py.
Mara Costa, a payments change_approver and not the author (Linh Nguyen), approved a code_review.
The code_review approval names head commit be74efa, the only commit on the change.

run.json reports success on head be74efa from ci-runner-07. However, the attached JUnit report is timestamped 2026-10-23, after the review time of 2026-10-15, and comes from host dev-laptop-7.local. So it is not credibly the CI run's report. Separately, the PR claims unit tests were updated, but no test file changed.
The only touched component, payments.retention, is not security_sensitive, so no security_review is required.
No protected paths (controls/, control tests, ci/) are changed, so no control_owner approval is required.
The ticket type is standard and the change is not marked emergency, so no PIR is required.
The ledger entries cover payments.py, audit.py, routes.py, Approvals.java, Underwriting.java and Policy.java. The change touches none of them, so no accepted evidence lapses.

summary: PR-1270 adds a rule that permanently exempts tax-authority payees from NPI disposal. That violates RET-1, which requires closed payee NPI to be purged after the approved retention period except under legal hold. There is no approved exception for RET-1 on payments.retention, so EXC-1 is also refuted. The ticket and approvals are in order, but the JUnit evidence is inconsistent with the CI run: it is dated after the review time and comes from a personal machine. The change is rejected.
